topPRs.title: op-reth: settle SDM refunds in block-level RPC replays
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Step 3 of the plan in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485, stacked on #23615: settle SDM refunds in the block-level RPC replays.

Pins reth to ethereum-optimism/reth#25, which moves reth's block replay loops behind defaulted `Trace` methods without changing their behavior. `OpEthApi` overrides them to replay through the block executor: `trace_block_transactions` (`trace_block`, `trace_replayBlockTransactions`, `trace_filter`, `ots_*` block traces), `debug_trace_block_transactions` (`debug_traceBlockByHash` / `ByNumber`, raw `debug_traceBlock`, `debug_traceBadBlock`), `debug_trace_chain_block_transactions` (`traceChain`) and `block_intermediate_roots` (`debug_intermediateRoots`).

`debug_traceBadBlock` goes through the executor too, so a bad block that the executor rejects (block gas, DA footprint, SDM refund-list validation) now fails to trace instead of tracing pre-refund. A bare-EVM fallback for that case is possible if we want it.

The regression test now also covers raw `debug_traceBlock` (canonical gas again, as in @pcw109550's repro on #485), `debug_traceBlockByNumber`, `debug_intermediateRoots` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions`. Those assertions fail without the overrides and pass with them; the op-reth `it` suite passes, clippy is clean and `just check-upstream-mirrors` passes.

**Do not merge yet:** the reth pin is the head of the unmerged ethereum-optimism/reth#25. Repin to the merged fork commit or tag, and move optimism-premium's reth pin in step.

topPRs.title: op-reth: settle SDM refunds on RPC replay paths
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
On SDM blocks, the RPC paths that replay a block's transactions report the pre-refund result: `debug_traceTransaction` / `debug_traceBlock*` return pre-refund gas and state diffs that charge the sender refund × price too much, `trace_*` state diffs and `eth_callMany` / `debug_traceCall` at an index / `debug_traceCallMany` start from unsettled balances, and `debug_intermediateRoots` never reaches the header's state root. Explorers and indexers ingest those numbers. With this PR every one of those paths agrees with the receipt, the committed balances and the header. Consensus, receipts and stored state are unaffected.

The settlement lives only in the block executor and the replay helpers live in reth, so the fix is ethereum-optimism/reth#18 (replay through the executor) and this PR pins it. `debug_trace_post_exec.rs` now sequences a real SDM block with the fixed test policy and checks each path; it fails on the current pin (every path off by exactly the refund × price split) and passes on this one.

Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485. The issue's last item — whether production SDM opt-in waits for RPC fleets to run this — is still open.

**Do not merge yet:** the pin is the head of the unmerged reth#18. Once it merges into the fork's `optimism` branch, repin all `rust/Cargo.toml` entries to the resulting commit and advance the `UPSTREAM-MIRROR` tags to it. optimism-premium pins the same reth rev and must move to that commit in step with its `optimism_rev`.

Behaviour changes that come with the fork change: a raw or bad block that fails the executor's per-transaction checks (cumulative gas, DA footprint, SDM entry validation) now errors in `debug_traceRawBlock` / `debug_traceBadBlock` instead of tracing, and replay errors map through `BlockExecutionError`, so their RPC error codes change. Neither is reachable when replaying a canonical block.

Review findings dismissed (please confirm):
- reth-update-reviewer: `eth_callMany`, `debug_traceCallMany`, `trace_block` / `trace_filter` and `ots_getTransactionError` are not exercised directly. They share `replay_block_until`, `trace_block_until_with_inspector` and `spawn_replay_transaction` with paths the test covers.
- rust-code-reviewer: prefer methods over free helpers. Not changed, because the sibling `invalid_post_exec.rs` uses free helpers.

topPRs.title: op-reth: settle SDM refunds in per-transaction RPC replays
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Step 1 of the plan in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485: fix the per-transaction RPC replay paths in op-reth alone, with no reth change.

On SDM blocks the RPC paths that replay a block's transactions run them on a bare EVM, so they report pre-refund gas and unsettled balances; only the block executor applies the settlement. `OpEthApi` now overrides `Trace::replay_block_until`, `Trace::inspect_transaction_in_block` and `Call::spawn_replay_transaction` to replay through the executor. That fixes `debug_traceTransaction`, `trace_replayTransaction` / `trace_transaction` / `trace_get`, `ots_traceTransaction` / `ots_getTransactionError`, and `debug_traceCall` / `debug_traceCallMany` / `eth_callMany` at a transaction index. The BAL argument these methods take is ignored: op-reth never caches a block access list.

Block-level paths (`debug_traceBlock*`, `debug_intermediateRoots`, `traceChain`, and `trace_block` / `trace_replayBlockTransactions` / `trace_filter`) are hard-coded loops in reth and still report pre-refund results. They need the reth extension points in ethereum-optimism/reth#25 and follow in a stacked PR.

`debug_trace_post_exec.rs` sequences a real refunded Lagoon block (moved from #23465) and checks the paths above against the receipt and the committed balances. It fails on `develop` (`debug_traceTransaction` gas 53006, receipt 53005) and passes here; the op-reth `it` suite passes and clippy is clean.

topPRs.title: ci,op-acceptance-tests: run SafeDB op-geth resync tests in dedicated jobs
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Follow-up to #23787, splitting the op-geth SafeDB resync step out of the sharded acceptance jobs as agreed in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23787#discussion_r4433552613.

The two resync cases SkipOnOpReth, so the sharded op-reth suite never exercises them. #23787 ran them as an extra step on shard 0 of each acceptance job, which `shard-tests.sh` cannot account for, so shard 0 was always longer by the full resync runtime. This moves the step into an `op-acceptance-tests` justfile recipe, `safedb-resync-test`, and runs it in two dedicated single-node jobs, `safedb-resync-opn-op-geth-fusaka` and `safedb-resync-kona-op-geth-fusaka`, on `xlarge.gen2`. Both are required by `ci-gate`, as the shard-0 step was before. The recipe keeps the `-run` restriction and the fail-on-skip guard, forces `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth` so it is also runnable locally, and writes the same `logs/<run>/summary.log` layout as `acceptance-test` so the job's result-printing steps work unchanged.

Based on `einar/safedb-remaining-validation`; retarget to `develop` once #23787 merges.

Validation:
- [x] Merged CircleCI config validates with `circleci config validate --org gh/ethereum-optimism`; all 23 `ci-gate` requires resolve to workflow job names.
- [x] `just --list` and `just -n safedb-resync-test` render; ShellCheck on the rendered body reports only the justfile's own backtick `REPO_ROOT` constant, shared with `acceptance-test`.
- [x] `go test -list` with the recipe's run filter selects exactly `TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync` and `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync`.
- [ ] CI: both new jobs green; shard 0 of the memory-all jobs no longer runs the resync step.
